cards.text: It's just before the Passover Feast. Jesus knows His hour has come to leave this world and return to the Father. And He has loved His own who were in the world.

cards.question: Jesus has loved His own who were in the world. How far does that love go?

cards.text: The evening meal is underway. But there's a dark detail about Judas, one of Jesus' disciples and the son of Simon Iscariot: the devil has already put something into his heart.

cards.question: What has the devil put into the heart of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot?

cards.text: Now here's what Jesus knows. The Father has delivered all things into His hands, and He came from God and is returning to God.

cards.question: Jesus knows all things are in His hands. True or false: He stays seated at the supper.

cards.text: He gets up from the supper, lays aside His outer garments, and wraps a towel around His waist. If somebody handed ME all things, friend, I'd call a press conference, and HE grabs a towel.

cards.question: Jesus pours water into a basin and begins to wash the disciples' ___.

cards.text: He dries them with the towel that's around Him. Then He comes to Simon Peter, one of His disciples, who asks, "Lord, are You going to wash my feet?"

cards.question: Jesus replies to Peter. True or false: Jesus tells Peter he will never understand what He is doing.

cards.text: Peter's answer: "Never shall You wash my feet!" That's me when a baker offers to scrub my mixing bowls: NO, no, no, I've GOT it.

cards.question: Jesus answers Peter. Unless Jesus washes him, what does Jesus say happens?

answers.text: Peter has no part with Him
Peter has to leave the room

cards.question: Peter hears that unless Jesus washes him, he has no part with Jesus. What does Peter ask for now?

answers.text: His hands and head washed too

cards.text: Jesus tells Peter that whoever has already bathed needs only to wash his feet, and he will be completely clean.

cards.question: Jesus has just told Peter that whoever has bathed needs only his feet washed. True or false: Jesus then says every one of the disciples is clean.
Jesus says not all of them are clean, because He knew who would ___ Him.

cards.text: When He's finished washing their feet, Jesus puts His outer garments back on and reclines with them again. Then He asks, "Do you know what I have done for you?"

cards.question: True or false: Jesus tells the disciples they're right to call Him Teacher and Lord.
Their Lord and Teacher just washed their feet. So what does Jesus say the disciples should do?

answers.text: Never let Him do it again

cards.text: Jesus says He has set them an example, so they should do as He has done for them. He didn't hand them a pamphlet on serving, friend; He handed them clean feet.
Jesus opens with "Truly, truly," and when He says it twice, I lean in. Then He tells them who is greater than whom.

cards.question: Jesus says no ___ is greater than his master, nor is a ___ greater than the one who sent him.
True or false: Jesus says the disciples will be blessed just for knowing these things.

cards.text: Then Jesus says He isn't speaking about all of them. He knows whom He has chosen.

cards.question: Jesus quotes Scripture about someone who "has lifted up his heel against Me." Who does it say that is?

answers.text: A servant of the high priest

cards.question: Jesus is telling them all this before it happens, so that when it comes to pass, they will ___ that He is He.

cards.text: One more "Truly, truly." Jesus says whoever receives the one He sends receives Him.

cards.question: Jesus says whoever receives the one He sends receives Him. And whoever receives Jesus receives whom?

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend. Supper's still going, and trust me, this night is not done.

findings.problem: Most story cards are plain retelling with no Papa Dorin voice. Only four cards carry a real comic beat (stop 1 cards 7 and 11, stop 2 cards 4 and 5). Stop 1 cards 1, 3, 5, 9 and 14 and stop 2 cards 1, 8 and 11 read like a flat summary of the verse. Examples: stop 1 card 14 'Jesus tells Peter that whoever has already bathed needs only to wash his feet, and he will be completely clean.' and stop 2 card 8 'Then Jesus says He isn't speaking about all of them. He knows whom He has chosen.' Some of these cards need his reactions, disbelief or storyteller lines.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Across both stops, Papa Dorin reads as mildly pleasant rather than laugh-out-loud funny. Many moments could hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, but they are left as plain narration: Jesus knowing all things and then grabbing a towel only gets one line, Peter swinging from 'Never' to 'my hands and my head as well', and Jesus saying 'Truly, truly' twice.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The card calls Judas 'one of Jesus' disciples'. John 13:2 doesn't say that, and the card cites only John 13:2. This fact comes from outside the verse (for example John 6:71, John 12:4) and has no reference.

rule.text: Every fact and every verse number comes from that text. Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke flips who is serving whom. Peter refuses to let his Lord serve him. In the joke, Papa Dorin refuses help from a baker who is helping him, and 'I've GOT it' reads as 'I'd rather do it myself.' That is a different action, and it hints at a motive for Peter that the text doesn't give.

rule.text: 2. The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The right answer 'His hands and head washed too' is a noun phrase. Both wrong answers start with 'To' ('To wash Jesus' feet instead', 'To be washed after supper'). Because the right answer is built differently, it stands out from the others.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card rewords John 13:19 'you will believe that I am He' into third person as 'they will ___ that He is He.' That reads unclearly and loses the 'I am He' wording. The card also says 'telling them all this' where the text says 'telling you now before it happens', which may widen what 'it' refers to.
findings.question: When a choice card puts Jesus' 'I am He' sayings into third person, should it quote the BSB wording ('believe that I am He') instead of rewording it as 'He is He'? Does 'all this' count as stretching an open 'it'?

findings.problem: The right answer 'The One who sent Him' echoes the question's own wording ('the one He sends'), and its capitalized 'One' marks God. The two wrong answers are almost the same as each other ('The prophet Isaiah', 'The prophet Elijah'). So the right answer is the obvious odd one out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The 'story isn't over' line copies the doc's example almost word for word ('And that's where we'll leave it for now... trust me... not done') instead of being a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
